structuralDecisions.decision: Switch @orieken/saturday-core, @orieken/saturday-cucumber and @orieken/saturday-playwright-heatmap in apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/package.json from file:./<dir> to workspace:*, matching the existing workspace:* entries already present for @orieken/saturday-playwright-k6-exporter and @orieken/saturday-playwright-leaflet in the same devDependencies block.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Confirmed by direct read of apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/package.json: two sibling framework deps in the same file already use workspace:*. This is the established pattern for every other Saturday package this app consumes — the three file: deps are the outliers, not a new choice. No new abstraction, package, or layer boundary is introduced; the dependency direction (app -> framework package) is unchanged and already correct.
tradeOffs: The app loses its ability to diverge from the framework package without that divergence being visible as a diffable change inside packages/ — this is the explicit goal of the feature, not a cost to mitigate.
Any future intentional per-app override of Saturday-core/cucumber/heatmap behavior must go through the package's own configure() API or a documented extension point, not a vendored fork.

structuralDecisions.decision: Fix the confirmed HEADLESS default drift inside packages/saturday-cucumber/src/config/index.ts (defaultConfig.browser.headless), changing the hardcoded false to process.env.HEADLESS === 'true', matching the vendored copy's already-correct behavior. Do not change any other field in SaturdayConfig or defaultConfig.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Read both files directly: apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/saturday-cucumber/src/config/index.ts:26 reads process.env.HEADLESS; packages/saturday-cucumber/src/config/index.ts:26 hardcodes false. Every other line in both files is byte-identical. This is the one behavior the package genuinely lacks, confirmed, not assumed.
tradeOffs: Changes the workspace package's default behavior for every consumer, not just this app — any other app currently relying on the package's unconditional headless:false default will start running headed unless it sets HEADLESS=true or overrides via configure(). No other in-repo consumer of packages/saturday-cucumber was found as part of this check; the developer should grep for other consumers before landing this.

fitness.property: packages/saturday-cucumber's default browser.headless value follows process.env.HEADLESS === 'true' (false when unset or any value other than the literal string 'true'), with no regression to any other defaultConfig field.
fitness.verification: packages/saturday-cucumber/tests/config.spec.ts (new) — vitest asserting getConfig().browser.headless reflects HEADLESS unset/'true'/'false' cases; must be shown to fail against the current hardcoded false before the fix lands, per the Test Repair Contract's rule for new tests.

componentPlacement.reason: This is the canonical location already — the vendored copy being deleted is a drifted fork of this exact file. No new layer or package is created; the fix lands in the file that already owns SaturdayConfig.
Mirrors the existing tests/ layout in the same package (coverage.spec.ts, world.spec.ts already live there); no new test directory structure needed.

crossings: apps/ye-olde-magic-shop (consumer app, outer/application layer for this feature's purposes) -> packages/saturday-core, packages/saturday-cucumber, packages/saturday-playwright-heatmap (framework packages) — the crossing already exists today via the vendored copies; this feature only changes the link from a drifted file: copy to a live workspace:* link. Direction of dependency (app depends on framework, never the reverse) is unchanged.

developerHandoffNotes: No RFC is being produced for this feature: the dependency switch matches an already-established in-file pattern (workspace:* for k6-exporter and leaflet), and the HEADLESS fix is a one-line default correction scoped to a single file plus one new test. Neither crosses a layer boundary that doesn't already exist, nor introduces a new abstraction. Reversibility: Cheap for both changes (a git revert fully undoes either).
